title: Full Stack Developer
description:
Role Summary
The Full Stack Developer is responsible for designing, developing, integrating, deploying, and supporting MOAM’s web, backend, and mobile applications. The role requires strong hands-on experience with .NET Core backend development and microservice architecture, Next.js frontend development, Flutter mobile development, and the infrastructure required to run these systems reliably in production.
The position will contribute to the design, development, and evolution of MOAM’s digital logistics ecosystem, including Courier and Cargo products across web and mobile platforms, shared backend services, system integrations, and future digital solutions, with responsibility spanning APIs, distributed services, caching, messaging, observability, databases, containerization, server administration, security, performance, and third-party integrations. The developer is expected to work across the complete software delivery lifecycle and collaborate closely with the Technology Unit and business stakeholders.

Duties and Responsibilities
A. Backend Development & Microservices
· Design, develop, maintain, and optimize backend services and REST APIs using C# and ASP.NET Core / .NET Core.
· Design services using microservice architecture, clear service boundaries, maintainable domain/application layers, and clean architecture principles.
· Implement authentication, authorization, role/permission management, API validation, error handling, background processing, and secure service-to-service communication.
· Work with SQL Server and relational data access using Entity Framework Core; design efficient schemas, migrations, indexes, transactions, and queries.
· Implement distributed caching and cache invalidation strategies using Redis or equivalent technologies.
· Use RabbitMQ for asynchronous messaging, event-driven workflows, queues, retries, and reliable communication between services; implement real-time application features using appropriate technologies such as SignalR/WebSockets where required.
· Integrate MOAM systems with ERP (including Sage), CRM, payment gateways, SMS/notification services, Firebase, customs systems, and other internal or third-party platforms.
B. Frontend Development
· Develop and maintain responsive, secure, production-ready web applications using Next.js, React, TypeScript, HTML, and CSS.
· Integrate frontend applications with backend APIs, authentication flows, real-time features, and server-side/client-side data fetching as appropriate.
· Build reusable UI components, handle application state effectively, and ensure performance, accessibility, maintainability, and cross-browser compatibility.
C. Mobile Application Development

title: Senior Database and Software Developer Associate – ACDMS
description:
Job Description
Under the overall supervision of the Senior Programme Coordinator (DTM) and the direct supervision of the National Information Management and Database Officer – ACDMS, and the technical supervision of the Database and Information Management Officer, the Senior Database and Software Developer Associate – ACDMS will be responsible and accountable for being the technical focal point for the database and application layers of the Afghanistan Centralised Database Management System (ACDMS). The role will support in the development, maintenance, integration, performance and operational reliability of the system. The incumbent will work closely with the ACDMS team, programme information management focal points, Information and Communications Technology (ICT) and other relevant units, and will work within agreed priorities and escalates only policy, strategic or exceptional matters.
ACDMS is a Country Office (CO)-wide institutional data management initiative intended to provide a centrally governed, secure, scalable and interoperable platform supporting beneficiary and service records, programme and project management, document management, referrals and case management, needs and assessments, monitoring and evaluation, audit functions, reporting and analysis. The platform is intended to reduce fragmented systems and duplication while strengthening data quality, accountability, information security and evidence-informed decision-making.
The position will translate approved functional specifications into reliable database structures, application components, Application Programming Interfaces (APIs), integrations, automated reports and technical documentation. Programme ownership, business-rule validation and prioritisation remain with the relevant programme management structures, while technical architecture, database standards and information management compliance will be guided by the Database and Information Management Officer.
Responsibilities
1.Develop, configure, maintain and support in the design of relational database structures, schemas, tables, views, functions, procedures and data models required for ACDMS modules. Apply approved naming conventions, data dictionaries, metadata and reference-data standards, and maintain technical consistency across development, testing and production environments.
2.Lead the configuration, maintainance and enhancement of secure web-based ACDMS applications and modules in accordance with approved functional and technical specifications to produce clean, documented and maintainable code, resolve defects, implement approved changes and steer controlled application upgrades and releases.
3.Develop and maintain approved application programming interfaces, data exchange services and integration routines connecting ACDMS modules with authorised internal or external systems. Conduct secure data migration, import, export, synchronisation and transformation processes with validation and reconciliation of migrated data.
4.Administer application source code, database scripts and related technical assets in approved version-control repositories applying agreed branching, peer-review, change-control, build and deployment practices, and maintain traceability between releases, approved requirements, test results and technical documentation.timise database queries, application components and reporting processes to improve performance, reliability and scalability. Undertake routine technical maintenance, identify emerging capacity or performance issues, and recommend technical improvements or implement approved corrective actions in coordination with the Database and Information Management Officer and ICT.
6.Implement and verify approved authentication, authorisation, role-based access, encryption, logging and audit-control requirements, apply secure coding and database practices, promptly document and escalate identified vulnerabilities or privacy risks, to uphold technical compliance with IOM information security and data protection requirements.
7.Prepare and conduct unit, integration, regression, performance and technical tests, document results and defects, support user acceptance testing led by the National Information Management and Database Officer – ACDMS, and verify approved acceptance criteria and release-readiness requirements before deployment.
8.Build and maintain approved automated reports, extracts, data services, dashboards and interfaces with business-intelligence or visualisation tools, document calculations, filters, data refresh routines and technical definitions, and align them with validated programme and information management requirements
9.Implement and test approved backup, restoration, disaster-recovery and business-continuity arrangements for ACDMS databases and applications, and maintain configuration records and technical recovery documentation in coordination with ICT and the Database and Information Management Officer.
10.Provide second-line technical support for ACDMS, diagnose and resolve application, database, integration and performance incidents, maintain clear incident and change records, and escalate issues requiring infrastructure, security, vendor or management action through the established channels.
11.Maintain and develop system architecture records, database diagrams, data models, API documentation, deployment instructions, configuration registers, release notes, code documentation and troubleshooting guides to facilitate structured knowledge transfer to other technical personnel and contribute to relevant technical training and user guidance.12.
Coordinate day-to-day technical work with the direct supervisor, the Database and Information Management Officer, ICT and assigned developers or assistants, provide technical guidance, code and database review, assign technical tasks, review outputs and support knowledge transfer and technical development of assigned personnel to foster aligned, quality-assured technical delivery and developed team capability.
13.Perform such other relevant duties as may be assigned.
Qualifications
EDUCATION
•Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology, Information Systems, Database Administration or a related field from an accredited academic institution with five years of relevant professional experience; or,
•High School diploma with seven years of relevant professional experience.
EXPERIENCE
Progressively responsible experience in database design, software or web application development, systems integration and technical support;
Experience developing and maintaining web-based applications using one or more established server-side and client-side programming languages or frameworks;
Experience developing or consuming RESTful APIs, web services or other data-integration mechanisms;
Experience using version-control platforms and structured software development, testing, release and change-management practices;
Experience implementing authentication, authorisation, role-based access, logging and other application or database security controls;
Experience with data migration, data validation, performance tuning, troubleshooting and production support; and,
Experience developing automated reports, dashboards or data services for business-intelligence and visualisation platforms is an advantage.

At WFP, people are at the heart of everything we do and the vision of the future WFP workforce is one of diverse, committed, skilled, and high performing teams, selected on merit, operating in a healthy and inclusive work environment, living WFP's values (Integrity, Collaboration, Commitment, Humanity, and Inclusion) and working with partners to save and change the lives of those WFP serves.

WFP invests in the personal & professional development of its employees through a range of training, accreditation, coaching, mentorship, and other programs as well as through internal mobility opportunities.
A career path in WFP provides an exciting opportunity to work across the various country, regional and global offices around the world, and with passionate colleagues who work tirelessly to ensure that effective humanitarian assistance reaches millions of people across the globe.
We offer an attractive compensation package (please refer to the Terms and Conditions section of this vacancy announcement).
BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE OF THE ASSIGNMENT:
The World Food Programme (WFP) is the world's largest humanitarian agency, fighting hunger worldwide. Over the years, WFP has made available its supply chain expertise, knowledge and network to governments, donors and UN agencies as a global good. The Data Scientist position will contribute to strengthening the evidence agenda of the Country Office through innovative analysis, including the development and training of artificial intelligence models tailored to food security and vulnerability, thereby enhancing the efficiency of VAM analysis and enabling more precise programme design and targeting

 Develop, test and refine geographical-level targeting criteria and models for emergency assistance, resilience, livelihoods and social protection interventions and geographical and beneficiary targeting to ensure maximum efficiency and equity in resource allocation, minimizing geographical bias.

title: Product Engineer (PM)
description:
Location: Fully Remote
Compensation: $23.08 to $34.62 USD/hour
Benefits: 15 days PTO. Christmas Day and New Year's Day paid off.
Fair warning: the pace is intense and the ambiguity is real. But you'll feel yourself growing every single week, even the rough ones, and you'll be doing it next to people who actually celebrate your wins and have your back.
We're the all-in-one agentic marketing platform. AI-native from day one. We're not joining a category, we're defining it.
We're looking for a Product Engineer to own a pod's output end-to-end: strategy, specs, QA, and enough technical depth to unblock engineers or write the code yourself when that's the fastest path forward. If you want real ownership, move fast, and raise the bar every week, keep reading. If you've been waiting for a PM role that doesn't ask you to leave your technical background at the door, this is it.
What you'll own
Own the roadmap for your pod: define what gets built, kill low-leverage work, and protect your engineers' time and focus
Write specs that start with the problem, not the solution, and ship every brief with a clear success criterion
Participate technically: read the codebase, debug independently, and ship small things when it's faster than context-switching an engineer
Own QA end-to-end: test plans, regression passes, release sign-off, and post-deploy monitoring in Sentry and Grafana
Keep the pod moving: fast decisions, async-first communication, and zero ambiguity about what's next
Close the feedback loop between customers, data, and product direction, and hold yourself accountable to the KPIs you define
You'll thrive here if...
You've shipped production code before and you're honest with yourself about your technical depth
You treat a spec as a hypothesis to pressure-test, not a document to execute against
You don't wait to be told what to do. You see the gap and you move.
Deadlines don't rattle you. Ambiguity doesn't either.
You're an AI power user, not someone who's "open to learning it someday."
You communicate clearly, especially when things are unclear.
You have opinions and you're not afraid to bring them.
You can laugh at a chaotic week on Friday and mean it.
What we're looking for
3+ years of product management experience in B2B SaaS, startup or high-growth environment
A hands-on technical background: production code, a bootcamp, or demonstrable ability to navigate a full-stack codebase
Comfortable reading Python and JavaScript/TypeScript; able to write SQL, reason about REST contracts, and follow frontend state
Proven QA ownership: test cases, regression cycles, structured bug reports, release sign-off
Daily fluency with Claude Code or equivalent. Not "open to it." Actually using it.
Strong written communication. Your specs are clear and complete on the first read.
Available in EST
What working here actually looks like
High expectations. Real ownership. Things change fast and we don't apologize for it. You'll work with smart people who push you, a product that keeps getting better, and a team that's genuinely building something new.
The boundary between product and engineering is intentionally blurred here. The best product decisions are inseparable from technical reality, and we hire people who understand that.
We'll probably give you more to own than you expected. That's on purpose.
We use AI every day, across every function. That's just how we work.
What we stand for
We are obsessed with our customers, and making them obsessed with us
We figure it the f**k out
We go to war on our problems quickly
We are strategic. We work smart, not just hard.
We're fun AF
About Search Atlas
Search Atlas helps marketing teams move faster, make smarter decisions, and do more with less. We're a $30M+ ARR company, 215 people, bootstrapped, and building the infrastructure for the next era of marketing. No outside funding. No fluff. Just product.

title: AI Experience Engineer (Conversational AI)
description:
Headquarters: Canada (Remote)
About the Role:
An AI Experience Engineer owns the full lifecycle of the journeys our customers have with Upgrade's AI agent on chat, voice and email: creation, optimization, edge case handling and containment growth. They build journeys in Sierra's no-code tooling, partner with Upgrade's product groups to bring their servicing flows to the agent, and are accountable for whether the agent resolves the customer's issue safely, accurately and without a human.
We are hiring an AI Experience Engineer to own Upgrade's customer-facing AI agent. You will sit between engineering, product and customer operations. You will turn servicing workflows, such as making a payment, checking loan details, updating an address or enabling autopay, into production journeys and keep improving them after launch. You will build and own the journeys end to end, from first draft to steady state. The work is part builder, part analyst: design the flow, handle the edge cases, read the transcripts, and keep raising containment. Containment, CSAT, transfer quality and hallucination rate are your metrics.
Within your first year, you will own a portfolio of journeys across products (Personal Loans, Card, BNPL, HELOC, Deposits) and help set the standards for how Upgrade builds, tests and ships AI experiences.
Our Core Technologies
Sierra Agent Studio (no-code journeys), Sierra simulations and conversation analytics, GraphQL and REST APIs (as journey tools), Genesys (contact center handoff), SumoLogic, Grafana, SQL, Javascript/Typescript, Claude and other LLM tools.
What You'll Do
• Journey creation: Design and build Sierra journeys in Agent Studio for chat, voice and email, from discovery with operations through production rollout
• Optimization: Review transcripts, recordings and analytics every week, find where conversations fail or transfer, and ship fixes to journey logic, instructions and knowledge
• Edge case handling: Map the unhappy paths (failed payments, mismatched identity, delinquent accounts, unsupported requests) and make sure each ends in a correct answer or a clean handoff
• Containment: Own containment and CSAT targets per journey, run staged rollouts (1% → 100%), and prioritize the work that moves those numbers most
• Product partnership: Work with product groups (Personal Loans, Card, BNPL, Deposits) to scope new journeys, keep journeys current as products change, and define the APIs the agent needs
• Safety and compliance: Apply tiered authentication and step-up verification, verbatim compliance language and guardrails against hallucination and off-policy answers
• Handoffs: Design transfers to human agents in Genesys with accurate summaries and auth context
• Testing: Build simulation and regression suites so every journey change ships with evidence it did not break existing behavior
• Monitoring: Watch latency, errors and drop-offs in SumoLogic and Grafana, and own the alerts
• Voice tuning: Latency, filler phrases, interruptions, personality and tone
• Sierra relationship: Be the technical owner on our side, escalate platform issues and shape roadmap asks
What We Look For:
• 3–5 years of Frontend Software Engineering experience, or equivalent experience in Solutions Engineering, Conversational AI or Technical Product roles
• Working knowledge of how LLM agents behave: instructions, tool calls, knowledge retrieval, and where each one fails
• Experience building evaluations for non-deterministic systems: test sets, simulations, LLM-as-judge, regression gates
• Enough technical depth to read API specs, work with backend engineers on REST and GraphQL integrations, and reason about authorization and permission scopes
• Working knowledge of JavaScript/TypeScript, with the ability to build and maintain coded journeys and integrate APIs within conversational AI platforms.

title: Software Engineer, AI Coding Tasks (Contract)
description:
Headquarters: Australia
URL: https://www.askablelabs.com/
We're looking for experienced software engineers to build AI coding tasks from a codebase they know well. US$1,000 per task, and you can do as many tasks as you want.
You turn a real change from a repository you know into a task that today's best AI coding models struggle with: hard for the models, but fair for a skilled engineer. Your tasks are used to measure and train AI coding models.
Remote, any location. US$1,000 per task that passes review. Minimum of one task a week, about 10 hours a week.
How it works
Apply. Complete a short screener interview and upload your resume.
Propose. Once you're selected, pick a change from a repository you know and submit a short proposal. We approve it or suggest a better candidate.
Build. In our platform, set up the repository as it was before the change, then write the brief, the correct solution and the grading checks.
Stress-test. Try lazy, incorrect and shortcut solutions and make sure your checks catch them.
Model testing. Run your task against leading AI models until strong models often fail but a skilled engineer can clearly solve it.
Review. A reviewer checks your task and you revise it. Most tasks take more than one round.
Next task. Once your task is accepted, start another.
Requirements
2+ years of professional software engineering
Code merged into a public open-source repository, ideally one you know well. A private codebase you own may also qualify (not employer or client code)
Strong in at least one of Python, TypeScript, Go, Rust, Java or C++
Solid with Docker, Linux, Git and automated testing
Regular use of an AI coding tool
Experience writing tests, rubrics or evaluation criteria, ideally for AI models
You can explain a change clearly and concisely, in your own words
At least 10 hours a week, starting now
A secure personal or work computer (no public or shared machines)
Nice to have
Deep expertise in one area, such as databases, compilers, distributed systems, security or infrastructure
Experience building agent tasks or RL environments
Terms
US$1,000 for each task that passes our quality review, paid directly to you
Once your proposal is qualified, you sign Askable's contract and accept its terms
The work is used for AI training. The change and your solution must be your own, and you must be free to license them to us
Don't publish the work anywhere: no public pull request or public fork

Dremio's Connectivity team builds the high-performance connectivity solutions that help customers bring data to Dremio and connect Dremio to the broader data ecosystem. title: Senior Security Engineer, Detection & Response
description:
Headquarters: U.S. Remote
About Flexport:
At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. That’s why it’s our mission to make global commerce so easy there will be more of it. We’re shaping the future of a $10T industry with solutions powered by innovative technology and exceptional people. Today, companies of all sizes—from emerging brands to Fortune 500s—use Flexport technology to move more than $19B of merchandise across 112 countries a year.
The recent global supply chain crisis has put Flexport center stage as we continue to play a pivotal role in how goods move around the world. We are proud to have the support of the best investors in the game who believe in our mission, solutions and people. Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us.
What you'll do
There is no MSSP and no tier-1 queue here. Detection & Response engineers own their detections end to end: you write them, you tune them, and your team is paged when they fire. The security team is spread across the globe with a follow-the-sun pager rotation so nobody is paged at 3am local.
The adversaries are real. The business is growing fast and the threat surface is growing with it. Defining the necessary telemetry is part of the job.
Detection engineering
Build and tune detections across endpoint, identity, SaaS, and cloud , treating them as software: version-controlled, peer-reviewed, and shipped through the same CI/CD practices the rest of engineering uses.
Track detection quality as measured quantities : coverage against MITRE ATT&CK, precision, time-to-detect. We don’t build-and-forget here.
Response & automation
Own incident response: triage, contain, remediate, and write the retrospective that turns the incident into a systemic fix.
Build automation that removes toil from investigations, and partner closely with the US-based team so context carries across time zones instead of getting lost at handoff.
Telemetry & partnership
Define telemetry requirements for new systems before they ship , working with infrastructure and product teams to close visibility gaps rather than discovering them during an incident.
Threat hunt proactively across the estate , converting hypotheses into either new detections or documented coverage.
You Should Have
Typically 5–8 years of experience in detection engineering, incident response, or threat hunting, with real hands-on time writing and tuning detections. We care more about what you've built than the exact number.
Proficiency in at least one programming language (Python, Go, or similar) and comfort writing production-grade detection and automation code.
Experience with a modern SIEM or detection pipeline (Panther, Elastic, Splunk, or similar). What matters is that you've shipped and tuned detection logic in production.
Practical incident response experience : you've led or played a major role in triaging and closing out real security incidents.
Nice to have
Experience treating detections as code with CI/CD, peer review, and staged rollout.
Experience defining telemetry contracts for systems before they ship, rather than retrofitting logging after an incident.
A track record of critically evaluating and verifying AI-assisted work - testing, source-checking, validation - rather than trusting agent output by default. If you haven’t already spotted the em dashes in this job description and already thought about where the hiring manager (hi!) has put hands on keyboard and compared that to where they let the LLM watermarks through, you might not be the right person for the job.
Familiarity with cloud-native and Kubernetes telemetry.
Experience with fraud or financial-crime detection patterns.
How we work
We stay closely aligned with teammates on other continents via Slack, video, and async docs.
We have the latest hardware and software, including frontier AI models on day one.
We're agile, but not dogmatic. Teams decide how they work best.

title: [REMOTE] Senior LiveOps Developer - Mobile Games
description:
Senior LiveOps Developer - Mobile Games
Remote - Full Time
CrazyGames , one of the world's largest browser game platforms with over 60 million monthly active users, is doubling down on its IP portfolio. We own the games we publish, and we treat each one as a live product rather than a finished project.
We're looking for a Senior LiveOps Developer who has already done this on mobile. Someone who has taken a title through soft launch and global launch, knows which live systems need to exist before you scale UA behind a game, and can build them.
This is a hands-on development role. You'll write the code for the events, the progression systems, the offers, the economy and the remote config that keep a game growing. You'll also be the person who looks at a game's numbers and says what should ship next and why, because you've run this playbook before at a mobile publisher.
What this role is not: greenfield game development, or working through a feature backlog someone else wrote. You'll be inside existing codebases almost all of the time, on games that already have players, and you'll be the one deciding what those games need.
Key outcomes for the role
Within 1 month , you've onboarded to one of our live published titles, gotten comfortable in its codebase, shipped your first live update to production on web and mobile, and given us your first read on what that game's LiveOps setup is missing.
Within 3 months , you own the LiveOps roadmap for at least one title. You've set an update cadence, shipped a meaningful live system (event framework, progression, offers, remote config, economy tuning), and we can see the effect in retention or monetization.
Within 6 months , you've taken a title through the run-up to global launch. The live systems, the event calendar, the balancing and the tooling are in place before UA scales behind it, and you decided what belonged there.
Within 12 months , LiveOps is a repeatable system across our IP portfolio rather than something that depends on you personally. Multiple live titles run in parallel on the cadence, tooling and playbook you put in place.
On a typical day you might
Look at retention, session length, ARPDAU and conversion for a live title, and decide what to build next.
Ship a seasonal event, content drop or offer to one of our live IP games on web and mobile.

description:
Shopware ist ein führendes E-Commerce-System , das es Unternehmen weltweit ermöglicht, im digitalen Handel schnell und effizient zu skalieren. Als zukunftsweisende Open-Source-Lösung wird Shopware bereits von einigen der größten europäischen Marken, Einzelhändlern und Herstellern im B2C- und B2B-Bereich eingesetzt.
Hilf dabei, Shopware-Produkte sicherer zu machen, indem du während der gesamten Produktentwicklung Sicherheitsrisiken aufdeckst und reduzierst. Du arbeitest mit den Produktentwicklungsteams daran, Schwachstellen zu untersuchen, sichere Konzepte und Tests zu verbessern und praxisnahe Maßnahmen aufzubauen, die wiederkehrende Probleme in Commerce Core, Services und angrenzenden Produktbereichen verhindern.
Product Security Engineering ist eine Engineering-Funktion . Die Produktteams bleiben dafür verantwortlich, ihren eigenen Code zu korrigieren und zu testen. Dieses Team bringt gezielte Sicherheitsexpertise, eine gemeinsame Roadmap zur Prävention und eine klare Koordination für produktübergreifende Sicherheitsarbeit ein.
Requirements
Untersuche Schwachstellenmeldungen, Sicherheitswarnungen, interne Findings und Nacharbeiten zu Sicherheitsvorfällen . Bewerte die technischen Auswirkungen und unterstütze dabei, bestätigte Aufgaben an die zuständigen Product Owner weiterzuleiten.
Arbeite direkt mit Entwicklerinnen und Entwicklern an sicherem Design, Threat Models, Code Reviews, Ursachenanalysen, Fixes und Regressionstests für besonders risikoreiche Produktbereiche.
Entwickle und verbessere wiederverwendbare Sicherheitskontrollen , Leitfäden für Entwicklerinnen und Entwickler, Tests für Missbrauchsszenarien und praxisnahe Automatisierung zur Erkennung und Behebung von Schwachstellen.
Unterstütze dabei, für Product-Security-Findings klare Verantwortlichkeiten, Schweregrade, Reaktionsziele, betroffene Versionen und Nachweise zum Abschluss festzuhalten.
Arbeite mit den Engineering-Teams von Commerce Core und Services an Sicherheitsaufgaben über verschiedene Repositories, unterstützte Versionen, APIs, Integrationen und das Extension-Ökosystem hinweg .
Unterstütze koordinierte Sicherheits-Releases : Ermittle betroffene Bereiche, prüfe technische Behebungen und stimme dich mit Engineering, Product Operations, Quality, InfoSec und DevRel ab.
Überführe Erkenntnisse aus Sicherheitsvorfällen und Releases in konkrete Änderungen am Engineering, Tests oder Tools. Verfolge anschließend nach, ob diese Maßnahmen übernommen werden.
Kommuniziere bei zeitkritischen Aufgaben klar und dokumentiere Entscheidungen in den vereinbarten GitHub- und Confluence-Einträgen, damit Teams den Status nicht aus Slack-Verläufen rekonstruieren müssen.
Wirke an gemeinsamen Teampraktiken mit und vertrete bei Bedarf den anderen Produktbereich.
Das bringst du mit:
Fundierte Erfahrung in der Softwareentwicklung und Interesse an Produkt- oder Anwendungssicherheit.
Praktische Kenntnisse typischer Risiken in der Anwendungssicherheit , etwa Schwachstellen bei Authentifizierung und Autorisierung, Zugriffskontrolle, Datentrennung, API-Sicherheit, Umgang mit Zugangsdaten, Injection und Abhängigkeiten.
Die Fähigkeit, produktiven Code und Tests zu lesen und zu ändern , Risiken für Entwicklerinnen und Entwickler verständlich zu erklären und wartbare Fixes mit umzusetzen.
Erfahrung mit Threat Modeling, Sicherheitstests, Schwachstellenanalysen oder Secure Code Reviews ; in einigen Bereichen bringst du fundiertes Wissen mit, in anderen möchtest du dich weiterentwickeln.
Gutes Urteilsvermögen bei der Einschätzung von Schweregrad, Auswirkungen auf Kundinnen und Kunden und Ausnutzbarkeit sowie bei der Frage, wann ein Problem sofort eskaliert werden muss.
Klare schriftliche Kommunikation und die Fähigkeit, bei unklaren oder dringenden Aufgaben teamübergreifend zusammenzuarbeiten.
Kenntnisse von PHP sowie mit Shopwares Produkten, Services oder dem Extension-Ökosystem sind hilfreich.

Design lead-to-cash capabilities spanning quoting, contracting, order workflows, service delivery, entitlements, renewals, and revenue-management integrations.
Build and maintain integrations between Salesforce and NetSuite, BigQuery, our contract-management platform, and other operational systems.

title: Computer Vision Engineer - Body Sensor Networks
description:
Do you get excited about building cutting-edge perception systems that work reliably in the real world? Do you have a strong foundation in computer vision, robotics, or sensor fusion? Are you interested in shaping new technology capabilities within a growing and innovative high-tech company, where people and fun are part of our core values? We’d love to have you!
Who is Xsens
Xsens is a leading full-stack provider of sensors, software, and analytics that enable the digitization of movement. Xsens serves entertainment, humanoid robotics, health & sports and automation & mobility markets. By turning complex motion data into actionable insight, we help our partners accelerate development, improve control and learning, and bring physically intelligent systems to life. We collaborate with leading global innovators including Boston Dynamics, Toyota, Siemens, Electronic Arts, Epic Games, Netflix, and 20th Century Studios, alongside more than 1,000 research institutions, humanoid robotics companies and universities worldwide.
Your role as a Computer Vision Engineer at Xsens
As a Computer Vision Engineer, you will lead camera-based perception for Xsens motion capture. Your role is to establish Deep Learning and Computer Vision pipelines to turn camera images into human pose estimate. You will learn from the highly-skilled team of sensor fusion experts, biomechanists and mathematicians. You will be its computer vision specialist, and report to the Technology Manager. The position is open to hybrid / remote working.
Key challenges:
Select, adapt and fine-tune deep learning models for 2D and 3D human pose estimation from cameras, that perform robustly in challenging real-world conditions.
Develop camera models and calibration routines for a range of camera and lens configurations.

description:
Join Tether and Shape the Future of Digital Finance
At Tether, we’re not just building products, we’re pioneering a global financial revolution. Our cutting-edge solutions empower businesses—from exchanges and wallets to payment processors and ATMs—to seamlessly integrate reserve-backed tokens across blockchains. By harnessing the power of blockchain technology, Tether enables you to store, send, and receive digital tokens instantly, securely, and globally, all at a fraction of the cost. Transparency is the bedrock of everything we do, ensuring trust in every transaction.
Innovate with Tether
Tether Finance: Our innovative product suite features the world’s most trusted stablecoin, USDT , relied upon by hundreds of millions worldwide, alongside pioneering digital asset tokenization services.
But that’s just the beginning:
Tether Power: Driving sustainable growth, our energy solutions optimize excess power for Bitcoin mining using eco-friendly practices in state-of-the-art, geo-diverse facilities.
Tether Data: Fueling breakthroughs in AI and peer-to-peer technology, we reduce infrastructure costs and enhance global communications with cutting-edge solutions like KEET , our flagship app that redefines secure and private data sharing.
Tether Education : Democratizing access to top-tier digital learning, we empower individuals to thrive in the digital and gig economies, driving global growth and opportunity.
Tether Evolution : At the intersection of technology and human potential, we are pushing the boundaries of what is possible, crafting a future where innovation and human capabilities merge in powerful, unprecedented ways.
Why Join Us?
Our team is a global talent powerhouse, working remotely from every corner of the world. If you’re passionate about making a mark in the fintech space, this is your opportunity to collaborate with some of the brightest minds, pushing boundaries and setting new standards. We’ve grown fast, stayed lean, and secured our place as a leader in the industry.
If you have excellent English communication skills and are ready to contribute to the most innovative platform on the planet, Tether is the place for you.
Are you ready to be part of the future?
About the job
We have launched Keet Mobile on iOS and Android, bringing our full P2P technology stack to everyone. Keet Mobile is not your average app: it’s heavy lifting is performed by a custom JS runtime specially designed for peer-to-peer usage (in fact, it reuses 100% of Keet Desktop’s code!). The UI logic, on the other hand, is 100% React Native, giving us flexibility and the ability to iterate quickly.
We believe this pattern opens the door to huge possibilities in the future, and we need your help getting there!
Responsibilities
In this role, you will develop and maintain Keet Mobile, our peer-to-peer chat and calling app for iOS and Android. Keet Mobile is built with React Native and Expo, and its P2P core runs on the device itself in a Bare worklet. You'll own features end to end, from UI/UX implementation to using the P2P core apis.
You will:
- Build and polish features across chat, voice and video calls, media sharing, device pairing and identity backup
- Integrate native platform capabilities such as push notifications, camera, bio-metrics and background tasks on both iOS and Android
- Profile and optimise performance on real devices, including startup time, long chats, media handling, battery and network use
- Write unit and end-to-end tests, and help keep releases stable through CI and crash reporting
- Work closely with the core P2P, design and product teams, and review code with a high bar for quality
Requirements
Significant experience with React Native, Redux for state management and Redux-Saga
Highly proficient in JavaScript and ES6+.
Experienced with WebSockets, RESTful based APIs.
Knowledge in native languages (Swift/Kotlin) and familiarity with native build tools (Xcode/Android Studio) is advantageous.

title: Principal Platform Engineer
description:
This is a hands-on engineering and technical leadership position. You will move fluidly between building production infrastructure, architecting multi-tenant isolation, designing pipeline and policy enforcement, leading strategic architecture decisions, and mentoring engineers. Your success is measured by what every product inherits: a compounding system that outlasts your direct involvement.
What You'll Do
Platform Architecture & Infrastructure Engineering
Drive the platform's architecture and runtime direction, including convergence onto one container-orchestrated runtime, tenancy-grade isolation between client engagements, and the contracts every product inherits.
Design composable infrastructure as code at fleet scale, with clear input contracts and state boundaries, published as versioned templates and images for every core component.
Make the environment lifecycle a one-command operation: created by merging a pull request, destroyed by deleting it, with automated proof nothing is left behind.
Design identity and network as a federated, credential-free system — one identity per engagement, just-in-time audited privileged access, separate internal and external edges.
Ship telemetry and cost visibility out of the box for every service: standard alerting, service-level objectives on live data, fault injection, and per-engagement cost attribution including AI spend.
Delivery Pipelines, Security & Compliance Engineering
Drive the shared delivery pipelines every product runs through, and the pluggable gate framework that quality, security, and AI-governance checks plug into with block-on-fail enforcement.
Implement security and compliance as code: release-blocking scanning on every repository, policy and admission control, signed and attested artifacts, and an audit trail and software bill of materials, including AI components, on every build as SOC2 / ISO 27001 evidence.
Package the AI-assisted development environment as a versioned, first-class deliverable, and enforce the sandbox boundary for coding agents: default-deny egress, short-lived credentials, isolated shared runners.
Run the platform as a product measured by developer outcomes — setup time, time to first commit, pipeline duration, gate false-positive rate, adoption — pruning or redesigning controls when governance burden outgrows benefit, and proving every golden path by shipping through it yourself.
Technical Leadership & Stakeholder Influence
Lead the platform's strategic architecture decisions — multi-tenancy, cloud posture, identity provider, network edge — as evidence-based decision documents with real trade-offs, and own the security and reliability evidence the program reports against.
Serve as a go-to technical authority on platform architecture and delivery engineering, consulted by senior stakeholders at the design and strategy stages, translating trade-offs and platform risk into actionable guidance, and mentoring engineers and vendor partners with observable improvement in design quality and production readiness.
What You'll Need
Required
15+ years in software engineering, platform or infrastructure engineering, or a closely related technical field.
Deep, hands-on expertise in infrastructure as code at fleet scale (Terraform or OpenTofu with Terragrunt or equivalent): module architecture, remote state, multi-environment topology.
Demonstrated experience operating multi-tenant Kubernetes platforms in production: GitOps, network and admission policy, workload identity, tenant isolation.
Proven track record building CI/CD as a shared platform (GitHub Actions or equivalent), with reusable workflow contracts, fleet-scale branch protection, and enforced quality and security gates.
Strong hands-on command of cloud identity and network security on Azure/AWS/GCP or a comparable hyperscaler: workload identity federation, RBAC, private networking, WAF, DNS.

Go Development: Write high-performance, resilient Go code to power the core logic of the vCluster platform.

Kubernetes Mastery: Deep expertise in Kubernetes internals. We value a profound understanding of how Kubernetes works (architectural patterns, networking, storage).

Builder Mindset: You build things outside of work. You have active GitHub projects, experiments, or open-source contributions that demonstrate your passion for building.
High Agency: You are highly technical and self-driven. You thrive in environments where you are expected to identify problems and solve them autonomously.
Start-Up Grit: Experience working in a high-growth environment. You are comfortable with ambiguity and eager to make an impact.
Bonus points for:
Community Contributions: A history of contributions to the Kubernetes project (Upstream), including documentation updates, Pull Requests (PRs), or active participation in Special Interest Groups (SIGs).
Startup Experience: You have been at an early-stage organization where you function autonomously and strive towards building something great.
About vCluster Labs
We're the #1 platform for AI infrastructure, trusted by the world's fastest-growing AI cloud builders. We're a venture-backed startup that's raised over $28M from top-tier investors including Khosla Ventures (first investor in OpenAI, GitLab, Stripe, and DoorDash), and we're in a hyper-growth phase looking for motivated people to join our team. Our headquarters are in San Francisco (Salesforce Tower), but our team is distributed around the globe with a remote-first culture.
We give AI Cloud providers and AI factories a hyperscaler-like experience on their own GPU infrastructure. Our platform runs the full stack an operator needs, from bare metal provisioning and node lifecycle management up through managed Kubernetes, Slurm, Ray, and inference clusters, so they can turn raw GPUs into cluster products they can sell in days instead of spending 12+ months building it themselves. Today we power over 100,000 GPUs and 1 million CPUs across 50+ AI clouds and Fortune 500 companies, backed by a team of 40+ infrastructure engineers who build alongside our customers rather than just shipping them software.
We're the company behind vCluster, the open source technology for tenant isolation on Kubernetes, with 11,000+ GitHub stars and 40M+ tenant clusters created since 2021. Open source is part of our DNA. At KubeCon North America 2025, we launched our Infrastructure Tenancy Platform for AI, a Kubernetes-native framework built for running AI, ML, and GPU-intensive workloads anywhere, with an NVIDIA-validated reference architecture for DGX systems.

title: Go Senior Software Engineer, AI Training
description:
Contract | Remote, worldwide | $100-$200/hour depending on experience and location | 10-20 hrs/week
Check out this Loom video for more details:
We're looking for highly experienced software engineer (SR+) to help evaluate the quality of interactions with modern coding agents such as OpenAI Codex and Claude Code.
This is not a traditional engineering role. You won't be writing production code. You'll be evaluating something harder: whether the model thinks like a great engineer.
What this role actually is
You will assess how AI coding agents behave in real-world scenarios, focusing on:
• Whether the response makes sense
Whether the preamble and reasoning are useful
Whether the output reflects strong engineering judgment
Whether the interaction feels right to an experienced developer
This role is about engineering taste. Syntax correctness is the easy part.
What you'll be doing
Evaluate AI-generated coding interactions end to end
Judge whether outputs are useful, correct at a high level, and aligned with how a strong engineer would think
Assess the quality of explanations and reasoning, not just the code
Distinguish between levels of response quality (what makes something a 2 vs a 4)
Give clear, opinionated feedback in writing on what worked, what didn't, and what felt off or misleading
Help define what great looks like when working with tools like Cursor, Codex and Claude Code
What we mean by "taste"
We're looking for engineers who can answer questions like:
Does this feel like something a strong engineer would actually say?
Is this explanation helpful, or just technically correct?
Is the model guiding the user well, or just dumping output?
Would this interaction build or erode trust?
You should be comfortable making subjective but rigorous judgments, and explaining them clearly.
Who you are
Senior, Staff or Principal-level engineer (or equivalent experience)
Strong background in TypeScript/JavaScript or Python
Hands-on experience with at least one of OpenAI Codex, Claude Code or Cursor
Deep familiarity with modern AI-assisted dev workflows
Able to evaluate code without executing it or reviewing every line
Strong written and spoken English (B2 or above). You'll be writing detailed feedback and recording short video explanations, so this is a hard requirement
Comfortable giving direct, opinionated feedback
High bar for what good engineering looks like
Nice to have
Prior exposure to prompt design or evaluation workflows
Experience mentoring senior engineers or defining engineering standards
Engagement details
Rate: $100-$200/hour depending on experience and location
• Hours: 10-20 hours/week, flexible
Duration: ongoing. Projects run from about two weeks to a few months each, and we offer new ones to evaluators who do well
Start: as soon as you clear the take-home and a project has an open seat
Process: one take-home evaluation exercise with a recorded Loom walkthrough. No interview

You will be supporting and maintaining the devices, servers and proprietary infrastructure that make up the core of the HeadSpin platform. Your primary responsibility will be responding to incidents and outages, both from proactive monitoring and from customer reports. This can include offline and unresponsive hardware and services, security incidents or other disruptions to HeadSpin services. You will manage the lifecycle of these issues from first report to resolution and handle appropriate escalation of issues to other teams within HeadSpin . The Support team at HeadSpin is part of our critical infrastructure and members of the team are expected to be part of an on-call rotation to provide continuous coverage for incidents.
HeadSpin values the unique knowledge provided by our frontline operations teams, your feedback on common issues, operational pain points, and processes will be key for the rapid growth of HeadSpin . You will be encouraged to give your input and help make our operations teams healthy and dynamic places to work.

Triage and respond to tickets relating to incidents and outages both generated by automated monitoring and customer reports

Participate in a responsive and accountable issue management process that can solve issues quickly, reliably and repeatability

Document workflow and playbooks for common issues and situations
Be part of maintenance and updates of critical software and network infrastructure
Assist with or recommend device deployments, upgrades and maintenance

Engage, collaborate, and communicate effectively with variety of stakeholders
Collaborate with remote team members to build and maintain positive, productive team relationships

0 to 2 year(s) (or equivalent) experience in a technical support role
Bachelor’s degree in computer science or comparable

title: QA and UAT Tester
description:
The QA and UAT Tester is responsible for ensuring that software releases meet functional, quality, and business acceptance requirements before reaching production, through rigorous manual and UAT testing. This is a defined growth role: the successful candidate is expected to progressively build test automation skills and contribute an increasing share of automated coverage over time, supported by structured training and mentorship, with a clear path toward a Test Automation Engineer profile as capability develops.
Test Planning & Case Design
Writes clear, traceable test cases and scripts from requirements, user stories, and acceptance criteria.
Maintains an organised, up-to-date test case repository aligned to current functionality.
Ensures test coverage maps back to requirements and identifies gaps before test execution begins.
Participates in requirement/acceptance-criteria reviews to raise testability concerns early.
Manual & UAT Test Execution
Executes functional, regression, and end-to-end test cycles according to the test plan.
Plans and coordinates UAT cycles with business stakeholders, including scheduling, scripts, and sign-off.
Documents test results, evidence, and outcomes clearly for audit and traceability.
Flags scope, environment, or data issues that put a test cycle at risk.
Defect Management & Reporting
Logs defects with clear reproduction steps, evidence, severity, and priority.
Tracks defects through to resolution and retests fixes before closure.
Maintains accurate defect status and communicates blockers or high-risk defects promptly.
Analyses defect trends to identify recurring problem areas.
Quality Gate & Release Readiness
Contributes to and upholds the team's Definition of Done and quality gate criteria.
Provides a clear go/no-go quality recommendation ahead of each release.
Escalates quality risks early rather than allowing them to surface at release time.
Maintains release-level test summary documentation for audit and stakeholder visibility.
Test Automation Skill-Building & Contribution
Actively develops automation skills through training, mentorship, and hands-on practice as part of an agreed development plan.
Contributes to and maintains automated test scripts for repetitive regression scenarios, with support from senior team members.
Progressively takes on greater ownership of automation as competence grows, moving from assisted to independent contribution.
Shares learnings and automation progress with the wider QA and development team.
Collaboration with Development & Product
Works closely with developers, Business Analysts, and the Product Owner to clarify requirements and acceptance criteria.
Participates in sprint planning, refinement, and review to provide a quality perspective early ("shift-left" testing).
Pairs with developers to understand root causes of defects and prevent recurrence.
Provides constructive, timely feedback on testability and edge cases during design and development.
Continuous Improvement & Documentation
Identifies and proposes improvements to test processes, templates, and tooling.
Maintains clear, current test documentation and a shared testing knowledge base.
Actively participates in retrospectives and follows through on agreed improvement actions.
Stays current with testing best practice and emerging automation tools/techniques.
Requirements
Bachelor's degree or diploma in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience).
ISTQB Foundation Certification (or equivalent testing certification) is advantageous.
1-3 years' experience in manual and/or User Acceptance Testing (UAT) within a software development environment.
Experience writing clear, traceable test cases and test scripts from requirements and acceptance criteria.
Experience executing functional, regression, and UAT test cycles and documenting results.

At Xogene, we’re revolutionizing the future of clinical trial transparency through AI-powered solutions. Join our team of experts who are transforming how leading pharmaceutical and life sciences companies navigate regulatory compliance. If you're driven by solving complex problems in a professional environment focused on meaningful and rewarding work, we want to hear from you.
POSITION OVERVIEW
Xogene combines regulatory expertise with advanced technology to automate complex processes in clinical trial transparency. Our software streamlines workflows through AI and agentic networking capabilities, improving data transformation and regulatory compliance for leading pharmaceutical and life sciences companies. We're committed to advancing technological solutions in clinical trial transparency.
As we continue to expand, we are seeking an experienced QA Tech Lead to drive our test automation initiatives and strengthen our testing strategy. Reporting to the Director of Engineering, the QA Tech Lead will own test automation strategy and execution.
This is a hands-on technical role: you will write and maintain automated tests while guiding the team's automation direction.
KEY TASKS AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Lead and mentor automation engineers, provide technical guidance to the wider testing team, and foster a culture of quality excellence and continuous improvement.
Support skill development across the team, including cross-training manual testers in automation (e.g., Playwright Codegen, low-code contributions, and AI-assisted scripting with tools such as Claude) and ensuring automation engineers understand product domain and end-user workflows.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams including Development, Customer Success, Product Management, Design and Product Support across multiple time zones.
Define the overall risk-based test strategy, focusing testing effort where regulatory and customer risk is highest, with clear criteria for which tests are automated, which remain manual, and what doesn't need a test at all. Own automation test plans and standards across all Xogene product releases.
Create and maintain quality metrics, KPIs, and dashboards on testing progress and potential blockers, and provide regular updates to the Director of Engineering.
Define test scope, objectives, success criteria, and time and resource estimates with stakeholders, and ensure comprehensive coverage through effective test case design and review.
Identify, assess, and mitigate quality risks throughout each sprint cycle, including during pre-release dry runs.
Architect, build, and maintain scalable automation testing frameworks, including our custom-built Playwright framework, enforcing code standards, and maximizing test reusability through the Page Object Model (POM).
Develop and execute automated test scenarios, scripts, and procedures for system, integration, regression, and API testing, growing automated test coverage across all Xogene software products.
Act as the technical point of contact and subject matter expert on the code and system architecture, diagnosing complex technical problems and designing solutions that reflect lessons learned.
Identify manual test cases suitable for automation and work with the Test Lead to prioritize and transition them.
Move automated suites from manual triggers to a tiered CI/CD strategy in GitHub Actions (Smoke, Sanity, and Nightly Regression) that serves as quality gates for developers, and maintain suite health, including resolving flaky tests and tracking automation coverage.
Oversee the integration between Playwright and Zephyr Scale, reporting test results directly into Zephyr Scale through automated JUnit XML reporting pipelines and maintaining a single source of truth for QA metrics.

We're looking for highly experienced software engineer (SR+) to help evaluate the quality of interactions with modern coding agents such as OpenAI Codex and Claude Code.
This is not a traditional engineering role. You won't be writing production code. You'll be evaluating something harder: whether the model thinks like a great engineer.
What this role actually is
You will assess how AI coding agents behave in real-world scenarios, focusing on:
• Whether the response makes sense
Whether the preamble and reasoning are useful
Whether the output reflects strong engineering judgment
Whether the interaction feels right to an experienced developer
This role is about engineering taste. Syntax correctness is the easy part.
What you'll be doing
Evaluate AI-generated coding interactions end to end
Judge whether outputs are useful, correct at a high level, and aligned with how a strong engineer would think
Assess the quality of explanations and reasoning, not just the code
Distinguish between levels of response quality (what makes something a 2 vs a 4)
Give clear, opinionated feedback in writing on what worked, what didn't, and what felt off or misleading
Help define what great looks like when working with tools like Cursor, Codex and Claude Code
What we mean by "taste"
We're looking for engineers who can answer questions like:
Does this feel like something a strong engineer would actually say?
Is this explanation helpful, or just technically correct?
Is the model guiding the user well, or just dumping output?
Would this interaction build or erode trust?
You should be comfortable making subjective but rigorous judgments, and explaining them clearly.
Who you are
Senior, Staff or Principal-level engineer (or equivalent experience)
Strong background in TypeScript/JavaScript or Python
Hands-on experience with at least one of OpenAI Codex, Claude Code or Cursor
Deep familiarity with modern AI-assisted dev workflows
Able to evaluate code without executing it or reviewing every line
Strong written and spoken English (B2 or above). You'll be writing detailed feedback and recording short video explanations, so this is a hard requirement
Comfortable giving direct, opinionated feedback
High bar for what good engineering looks like
Nice to have
Prior exposure to prompt design or evaluation workflows
Experience mentoring senior engineers or defining engineering standards
Engagement details
Rate: $100-$200/hour depending on experience and location
• Hours: 10-20 hours/week, flexible
Duration: ongoing. Projects run from about two weeks to a few months each, and we offer new ones to evaluators who do well
Start: as soon as you clear the take-home and a project has an open seat
Process: one take-home evaluation exercise with a recorded Loom walkthrough. No interview

Analyze NCCL and distributed workload results with compute engineers to isolate communication bottlenecks and improve multi-node performance.
Use telemetry, switch counters, fabric management platforms, and diagnostic tools to identify degraded links, optical issues, packet loss, or unexpected congestion.
Own networking acceptance evidence, defect remediation, configuration sign-off, and readiness recommendations for commercial service.

Provide senior technical escalation for production incidents involving fabric instability, host connectivity, network performance, routing, or persistent hardware faults.

IOMETE is the sovereign data platform for the AI era. Enterprises run our data lakehouse, built on Apache Spark and Apache Iceberg, in their own trusted environment: on-premises, in their own cloud, or hybrid. It is built for regulated industries such as financial services, healthcare and government. Customer data never leaves the customer's trust perimeter, and the AI we build on it stays inside that perimeter too.
Position overview
We are seeking a highly skilled and motivated AI Software Engineer to join our team. We tackle a variety of exciting challenges, from connecting AI tools and models to the lakehouse to diagnosing Spark applications and troubleshooting failures. You'll build agents that run inside the customer's environment, on LLMs the customer provides or, later, on custom models we train for Spark tuning and troubleshooting. You'll also build the framework that defines those agents and the harness that runs, limits, traces and evaluates them.
The AI team
We are building the AI platform for the lakehouse — Lakehouse Intelligence. The team's roadmap includes, but is not limited to, the MCP Server for AI Agents, which lets AI tools query the lakehouse; the Model Gateway, through which IOMETE 's AI features call models; agents for Spark application diagnosis, troubleshooting and onboarding; and SQL AI Functions, which run language models from inside a query. Down the road, you'll also get to fine-tune and build custom models for our platform's specific needs, small enough to run inside a customer's deployment.

title: DevOps Engineer (Vac DST)
description:
About Logos (λ)
Logos (λ) is a movement of technologists, creatives, strategists, and activists working together to build a sovereign, people-owned technology stack that revitalises civil society and protects digital liberties at scale.
This position is within the IFT Technical Services (IFT-TS) Distributed Systems Testing (DST) Team, a team that primarily supports Logos, while also contributing to other IFT projects.
The role
We are seeking an experienced Distributed Systems Evaluation Engineer to join the Institute of Free Technology - Technical Services, on the Distributed Systems Testing (IFT-TS DST) team. This role focuses on rigorously assessing the performance and reliability of IFT projects at scale, where Logos (λ) is one of them.
Logos (λ) technology stack is composed of 3 main components:
Logos (λ) Blockchain : Advanced privacy for a new era of decentralised applications and social institutions.
Logos (λ) Messaging : Private peer‑to‑peer communication that resists surveillance and censorship.
Logos (λ) Storage : Secure decentralised storage enabling fully decentralised apps and file sharing.
We are looking for a talented and enthusiastic DevOps Engineer to join our Distributed Systems Testing (DST) team.
You’ll be responsible for designing and executing comprehensive evaluation strategies, leveraging both large-scale lab deployments and protocol behavior modeling scripts. Your expertise will be crucial in analyzing these complex distributed systems, automating intricate test scenarios, and providing in-depth insights into system behaviors.
Working closely with cross-functional teams, you’ll troubleshoot complex issues and translate technical data into actionable recommendations. Proficiency in containerization, cloud technologies, and distributed systems principles is essential.
Key responsibilities
Design, configure, and optimize Kubernetes clusters to support large-scale experiments and benchmarks of P2P technologies.
Continuously improve cluster scalability and resource utilization, enabling increasingly complex deployments and experiments.
Set up, maintain, and optimize supporting infrastructure such as monitoring, logging, and observability stacks (Grafana, Prometheus, Loki, etc.).
Collaborate with DST researchers and engineers to streamline experimentation workflows and make analysis easier and more reproducible.
Automate infrastructure and deployment workflows to increase reliability and reduce overhead.
Troubleshoot, profile, and tune distributed workloads to ensure accurate and performant benchmarking.
Identify, reproduce, and debug complex issues in distributed systems, working closely with Logos development teams.
You ideally will have
Strong experience with Kubernetes and container orchestration in production or research environments.
Solid understanding of cloud infrastructure, Linux systems, and networking (especially relevant to distributed/P2P systems).
Familiarity with monitoring and logging tools (Grafana, Prometheus, VictoriaLogs, etc.).
Experience with infrastructure as code (Terraform, Ansible, Helm, etc.).
Proficiency in at least one scripting/programming language (ideally Python).
Interest in or experience with distributed systems, P2P networks, or blockchain technologies.
Experience with networks and systems programming.
Excellent written and conversational communication skills.
Alignment with our core values and principles.
Bonus points
Hands-on experience with libp2p or projects in the Logos collective.
Background in performance benchmarking, scalability testing, or systems research.
Contributions to open source projects.
Experience working for an open-source organization.
Interview Process
Interview with our POps team
Interview with team member from the IFT-TS DST team
Take-home assignment and discussion of results
Interview with IFT-TS team lead

title: Junior DevOps Engineer
description:
The Junior DevOps Engineer builds foundational DevOps skills by supporting the maintenance of CI/CD pipelines, assisting with monitoring and alerting, and helping with basic infrastructure, access, and security administration tasks, all under the close supervision of more senior engineers. The role is expected to grow steadily in independence and technical scope as competence and confidence increase across the toolchain and internal platforms.
CI/CD Pipeline Support
Assists with the maintenance and minor configuration changes of existing CI/CD pipelines under guidance from senior engineers.
Monitors pipeline runs, flags failures, and helps triage straightforward build/deploy issues.
Follows documented runbooks and change procedures when making pipeline adjustments.
Escalates ambiguous or higher-risk pipeline changes to a senior engineer before proceeding.
Monitoring & Alerting Assistance
Helps configure and maintain basic monitoring dashboards and alert rules under supervision.
Performs first-line review of alerts and escalates genuine incidents promptly to senior engineers.
Documents recurring alert patterns and contributes observations to runbook improvements.
Learns the organisation's monitoring stack (e.g., Prometheus, Grafana) and standard thresholds.
Basic Infrastructure & Environment Tasks
Assists with routine infrastructure tasks (e.g., environment provisioning support, configuration updates) under close supervision.
Follows infrastructure-as-code templates and change processes rather than making ad-hoc changes.
Documents steps taken and outcomes for tasks performed, to support knowledge transfer.
Builds working familiarity with core cloud services and infrastructure tooling used by the team.
Access, Security & Platform Administration Support
Assists with routine access management tasks (e.g., user provisioning/de-provisioning) following approved processes.
Supports basic security hygiene tasks such as patch tracking and access reviews under supervision.
Helps administer internal platforms (e.g., Bitrix24 and similar internal collaboration/CRM tools) for routine, well-defined requests.
Escalates any anomalous access requests or potential security concerns immediately.
Ramp-Up and Learning Velocity
Actively works through onboarding materials, toolchain documentation, and internal platform guides.
Pairs frequently with senior DevOps engineers to build understanding of pipelines, infrastructure, and security practices.
Tracks own learning goals and progress with support from a mentor or the DevOps Lead.
Builds toward taking on progressively larger and less-supervised tasks.
Adherence to Standards and Process
Follows documented change management, security, and operational procedures without bypassing approval gates.
Uses agreed tools and ticketing systems consistently and accurately.
Applies feedback from senior engineers and the DevOps Lead consistently in subsequent work.
Raises process gaps or unclear documentation to the team rather than working around them.
Requirements
Bachelor's degree or diploma in Computer Science, Information Technology, Software Engineering, or a related field, OR a completed relevant bootcamp/certification path with a demonstrable practical portfolio.
0-2 years' experience in a DevOps, systems administration, or software development support capacity.
Basic understanding of version control (e.g., Git) and branching workflows.
Exposure to Linux/Windows server environments and basic scripting (e.g., Bash, PowerShell, Python).
Some exposure to CI/CD concepts and tools (e.g., Jenkins, GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps Pipelines).
Basic understanding of networking fundamentals (DNS, TCP/IP, HTTP/HTTPS).

Als Architect oder Technical Lead bist du verantwortlich für die Auswahl und Implementierung geeigneter Technologien, die Sicherstellung der Datenintegrität und -sicherheit, sowie für die effektive Zusammenarbeit mit anderen Teams und Stakeholdern, um die Kundenziele durch datenbasierte Lösungen zu erreichen.

Python, SQL, Java
Relationale und NoSQL-Datenbanken
FastAPI, Flask
Databricks, Spark, Kafka, Airflow, dbt, BigQuery oder Snowflake
AWS, GCP, Azure
Docker, Kubernetes
Intern wie extern kannst du dich bei uns auf vielfältige Art einbringen: Deinen anfangs gewählten technologischen Schwerpunkt kannst du jederzeit verlagern. Als erfahrener Engineer hast du außerdem die Möglichkeit, jüngere Kolleg:innen durch Mentoring zu unterstützen.
Requirements
Wer gut zu uns passen würde
Du hast ein abgeschlossenes Studium im MINT-Bereich oder in einem vergleichbaren Studiengang und bringst bereits mehrere Jahre Berufserfahrung und fundierte Kenntnisse in einem Großteil der oben genannten Technologien mit.

In der schnelllebigen AI & Data Tooling-Landschaft behältst du den Überblick. Du weißt neue Technologien einzuordnen und sinnvoll sowie effizient in bestehende oder neu aufzubauende Datenservices zu integrieren.

Perena is a decentralized financial protocol on Solana that offers USD STAR (USD*), a yield-bearing asset. USD* is fully collateralized and earns yield from diversified, real sources such as delta-neutral strategies and secured borrow-lend market positions. Its value grows automatically, making it a simple, secure way to save on-chain.

Looking ahead, Perena is building a full suite of on-chain stablebanking products to expand access to real yield across crypto and traditional finance. The goal is a sustainable financial experience for anyone to transact, save, and invest on-chain.

title: Senior Backend Engineer
description:
Senior Backend Engineer
About us
We're creating the foundational backend systems that power private market access, from secure authentication and transaction processing to portfolio management and regulatory compliance.
The Role
We're looking for a Senior Backend Engineer to own the systems where money moves and balances have to be correct — the ledger, transaction processing, and the settlement and reconciliation workflows behind our platform. This is the correctness core of what we build. If a balance is wrong, a transaction double-processes, or a reconciliation silently drifts, nothing else we build matters.
You'll design the double-entry ledger, the money-movement engine, and the long-running state machines that carry complex financial workflows to completion reliably over hours, days, or weeks. You'll reason about idempotency, concurrency, partial failure, and replay as a matter of habit, not as an afterthought.
You'll own core infrastructure decisions and set the standard for how we build financial systems.
Requirements
What You'll Do
Design and build the double-entry ledger and money-movement engine that all transactions reconcile against
Model complex financial workflows as robust, observable state machines that run reliably over long periods
Guarantee financial correctness under concurrency: idempotent operations, transactional integrity, and reconciliation that ties out to the cent
Handle partial-failure and replay cases so no event is lost, duplicated, or applied twice
Build secure, well-versioned APIs
Design and optimize PostgreSQL schemas and data models
Debug production issues and own the reliability of mission-critical financial workflows
What We're Looking For
5+ years of backend development on production systems
Demonstrated money-movement correctness experience: you've built a ledger, settlement system, payments core, or transaction-processing system and can talk in detail about how you kept it correct
Concurrency and idempotency depth: you can explain, from experience, how you handled double-processing, race conditions on balances, and replay
Reconciliation experience: you've built or owned systems that had to tie out exactly, and you know what happens when they don't
Strong TDD practices: you write tests first and maintain comprehensive coverage
Domain-Driven Design expertise: you model complex financial domains accurately
Deep PostgreSQL knowledge: schema design, transactions, isolation levels, optimization
Strong in a modern backend stack: we work in TypeScript/Node.js, Go and on the JVM ecosystem; we value real depth in either and the range to pick up the other
• Cloud deployment experience
Startup mentality: comfortable with ambiguity, high autonomy, driving solutions without detailed specs
Nice to Have
Payments, banking, brokerage, or investment-platform systems experience
Securities, custody, or portfolio/NAV domain knowledge
Event-driven architectures and message queues
Infrastructure as Code (Terraform, CloudFormation)
Understanding of KYC/AML or compliance frameworks
Accounting principles or financial modeling

title: Senior Software Engineer
description:
This role is part of our ScraperAPI team, one of our growing brands at saas.group .
ScraperAPI is an enterprise-scale web scraping solution, trusted by businesses across a wide range of industries to extract crucial data at scale. From e-commerce, travel to real estate and market research, we support companies in turning the web into actionable insights. We're currently on an exciting growth journey, scaling rapidly as demand for reliable, high-performance web scraping and data keeps rising.
Profile Overview
This is the hard end of web scraping. The sites we rely on, Google, Amazon, Walmart and many others, actively work to block us, and they change the rules without warning. We're looking for a senior engineer who can go deep on why we're being blocked, work out how the detection actually functions, and design repeatable ways around it. You'll be joining a self-driven, high-autonomy team to take on our most involved problems, with the room and the trust to build something from close to a blank page: an environment that turns one-off breakthroughs into a methodical, repeatable way of defeating anti-bot systems. If you like confronting problems that genuinely resist you, and you work methodically rather than by trial and error, this is an unusually open brief.
Your immediate impact in the first 3-6 months will be:
Getting a full local environment running and becoming fluent in our systems and how they operate, in the first few weeks.
Contributing to a proposal on the design for a repeatable environment we can pose anti-bot problems to and get reliable analysis out of.
Building that environment out over the following months so that, by month six, we can point it at a target or provider and have it reliably tell us how we're being blocked and what is and isn't being used against us.
Your responsibilities
Analyse how specific anti-bot and bot-mitigation systems (the likes of DataDome, Cloudflare Turnstile, Kasada, PerimeterX and Akamai) detect and block us, and design systems to work around them.
Turn isolated breakthroughs into durable, repeatable processes: hypothesis, test, discard what's wrong, move on.
